recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a future Patient Care decision intentionally changes AdverseEvent ordering semantics or the FiveWs model is renamed again.
issue_request: FHIR-22737 was a Published FHIR-core Patient Care change request for the AdverseEvent resource. The QA warning said elements were out of W5 order and the persuasive-with-modification resolution required AdverseEvent.subject to be treated as who.focus so it sorts after event/code and before encounter.
initial_application: The issue was applied in 19edc88a0ded155ed3e803b73666a87dc384f4bb, a multi-issue AdverseEvent QA commit that explicitly named GF#22737 and changed the old spreadsheet's AdverseEvent.subject W5 mapping from who to who.focus. The 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 source rework moved the resource to structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml while preserving the subject-before-encounter ordering.
additional_context: Later AdverseEvent Jira work renamed or refactored related elements: event became code, date became effect[x], resultingCondition became resultingEffect, severity was removed, and contributor/detector-style participation moved under participant-related structures. Later W5 cleanup commits ab7d0088743cb638033cd9a214779cd3c9a0bdcc and cd774234a5b73a2f28165e4393cb681715233c43 explain why the current AdverseEvent mapping is represented as FiveWs.subject rather than the older generated FiveWs.subject[x] form. The FiveWs source defines FiveWs.subject as who.focus.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent in the active build, and source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml currently orders code, subject, encounter, effect[x], recordedDate, and recorder consistently with the FHIR-22737 intent. AdverseEvent.subject maps to FiveWs.subject, whose current FiveWs definition carries the requested who.focus semantics.
